title: Bathroom scouring paste
subtitle: A thick bicarbonate paste for sinks, baths, and tiles
excerpt: A mildly abrasive paste of bicarbonate of soda, Castile soap, and tea tree essential oil. Cleans sinks, baths, shower trays, and grout without scratching glazed surfaces. Makes about 300 g.
sourceNotes: Bicarbonate of soda abrasive action and compatibility with glazed ceramic surfaces: open-access data from the Soap and Detergent Association (cleaninginstitute.org). Tea tree oil antimicrobial activity: Carson, C. F. et al., 'Melaleuca alternifolia (Tea Tree) Oil: a Review', Clinical Microbiology Reviews (2006, open access). Castile soap as surfactant base: formulation references in classic natural cleaning literature.

recipe.yieldDescription: ~300 g paste (roughly 30 cleaning applications at 10 g per surface)
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles easily; store in a second jar.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Makes quickly as needed; shelf-stable for six months.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Keeps six months in a sealed jar in the bathroom cupboard. Discard if the paste dries out completely, turns grey, or develops an off smell. If the paste separates slightly, stir to recombine.

glossaryTerms.definition: Bicarbonate of soda is a class 2 abrasive: fine enough not to scratch glazed ceramic or enamel, but coarse enough to dislodge soap scum and mineral deposits when rubbed with a cloth.

content.text: Weigh the bicarbonate of soda into a bowl.
Add the essential oils and stir to distribute.

Add the Castile soap a little at a time, stirring as you go. Stop when the mixture reaches a thick, spreadable paste. It should hold its shape when scooped with a spoon but spread easily under a cloth.
Spoon into a wide-mouth glass jar. Cover with a lid.
Scoop a small amount onto a damp cloth or sponge. Rub in circles over the surface. Leave for one to two minutes on stubborn staining. Rinse thoroughly. For grout lines, apply with an old toothbrush.

Safe on glazed ceramic, porcelain enamel, stainless steel, and chrome. Not for natural stone (marble, limestone, granite), soft enamel, or acrylic baths (test a small patch first). Not for sealed or oiled wood surfaces.
Keeps six months in a sealed jar. If the paste thickens over time as the soap dries, stir in a few drops of water. Discard if mould appears or the paste smells off.
